# Value at Risk (historical, 95%) (`var_historical_95`)

*Category: Tail behavior · Nature: estimated · Unit: decimal_return · Formula id: `var_historical_95@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Return threshold that was breached in the worst 5% of periods.

## 2. Formula

```text
Q_0.05(r), empirical quantile with linear interpolation (Hyndman-Fan type 7)
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

In about 1 period out of 20, the return was this bad or worse.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Historical-simulation VaR at 95% for one observation period; says nothing about losses beyond the threshold (see Expected Shortfall).

## 7. Assumptions

- The supplied history is representative of the tail.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Few observations fall in the 5% tail: with monthly data a 95% estimate rests on roughly n/20 points.
- The history does not contain a stress period.
- Returns are smoothed, which compresses the tail.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 observations; low confidence when fewer than 5 observations are expected in the tail (n < 100). (policy `tail`: Requires at least 2 observations; low confidence when fewer than 5 observations are expected in the 5% tail (n < 100), moderate when fewer than 10 (n < 200).)

## 10. Reference implementations

| Library | Function | Agrees | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| PerformanceAnalytics 2.0.4 (R) | `VaR(p=0.95, method='historical')` | yes | Reports the negated quantile (loss as a positive number in 2.0.4 internals, negative in the public wrapper). |
| NumPy | `quantile(method='linear')` | yes |  |
| QuantStats 0.0.81 | `stats.value_at_risk` | no (documented difference) | QuantStats defaults to a parametric (normal) VaR. |

## 11. Sources

- Jorion, P. (2006). Value at Risk (3rd ed.). McGraw-Hill.
- Hyndman, R. J., & Fan, Y. (1996). Sample Quantiles in Statistical Packages. The American Statistician, 50(4), 361-365 (definition 7 = linear interpolation).

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

95% confidence, per observation period, signed return (negative = loss), linear interpolation (decision 0010).
